title: Gene regulation and the trp operon

draft.title: Gene regulation and the trp operon
card: Bacteria can switch genes on or off, so they only make proteins they need. Making unneeded proteins wastes energy.
The trp operon is a group of genes in bacteria such as E. coli. The genes code for enzymes that make the amino acid tryptophan.
the repressor protein is inactive and cannot bind the operator, a DNA section next to the genes. RNA polymerase can transcribe the genes, so tryptophan is made.
tryptophan binds the repressor and activates it. The repressor binds the operator and blocks RNA polymerase, so the genes are switched off and energy is saved.
draft.remember: Plenty of tryptophan activates the repressor, which blocks transcription of the trp genes.

a.q: What does tryptophan do in the trp operon when it is plentiful in the bacterial cell?
opts: Binds the repressor so it blocks the operator
Binds RNA polymerase so it copies the genes faster
Destroys the operator so the genes cannot be read
Stops the repressor being made in the cell
a.why: Tryptophan binds the repressor and activates it, so it sits on the operator and blocks transcription. It does not speed up RNA polymerase, because the genes are switched off.
a.clue: Tryptophan acts on the repressor protein.

b.q: A mutant E. coli has a repressor that cannot bind the operator, even with tryptophan present. What happens to its trp genes in a tryptophan-rich medium?
opts: They keep being transcribed, wasting energy
They are switched off, as in normal E. coli
They are never transcribed, so tryptophan runs out
They are transcribed only when tryptophan is low
b.why: The repressor cannot block the operator, so RNA polymerase keeps transcribing the genes even though tryptophan is plentiful. Enzymes are made that are not needed, which wastes energy.
b.clue: Without a working block, what stops RNA polymerase?

a.best: Binds the repressor so it blocks the operator

b.best: They keep being transcribed, wasting energy

check.summary: No problems found. The card correctly describes the repressor model of the trp operon, both questions have one clear right answer, and the explanations match the card.
